findings.label: F-2-007 answered: the apps match is exact and case-sensitive, a prefix is a different name, and the fail-closed default writes an empty template list without reading the source config, so no normalisation bypass exists.
F-2-007: the plan has no name-in-words rule for a displayed tool name, the exact failure OpenBot found live when a line read web_search.
F-2-007: the 64-character provider cap forces a shortened name with a hash and the plan has no mapping back, which bites the 001 activity row rather than the 007 filter.

F-2-008 answered: the plan refuses --scope always outright and bots enable records scope once, so there is no standing answer to save and the three OpenBot exclusions bind only the phase that adds one.
F-2-009 correction: the plan detail is a fixed phrase per cause, so iteration 1 finding 7 is refuted; what survives is that the rule is stated by example in a design file and not as a contract line.
F-2-009: the plan already measured the echo it guards against, an over-long security line writing a wrong value to the wrong keychain and printing part of the value to stderr.
006: the plan grant holds four fields and has no place for the effect class, so a flow-scoped grant cannot be expressed and 006 should record it as out of scope.
007: the checker imports the same predicate the runner calls, the one-declaration pattern OpenBot uses, and 006 and 008 each carry their own copy of the rule instead.
008: the plan fails closed on every surface and never falls back to the environment-only map, which is stronger than rakazo isDevSecretAllowed and should be cited as the counter-example.
006: the reference composes checks, a host-tool check never relaxing a path or command check beside it, and the plan ladder applies at one gate so two checks on one call cannot compose.

proposals.question: Does the plan activity row have a rule for a tool name that a provider shortened to 64 characters, and what does the row show when the whole name is unknown?
